segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Setting out from there, he came into the region of Judea and beyond the Jordan, and crowds again gathered around him, and as his custom was, he again taught them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they asked him whether a man is allowed to divorce his wife, testing him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What did Moses command you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of dismissal and to divorce her.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “It was because of your hardness of heart that he wrote this commandment for you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But from the beginning of creation, ‘he made them male and female.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Therefore what God has joined together, let no human being separate.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In the house again, the disciples asked him about this.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: People were bringing children to him so that he might touch them, but the disciples rebuked them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus saw this, he was indignant and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Let the children come to me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he was setting out on the road, a man ran up, knelt before him, and asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one: God.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not give false testimony. Do not defraud. Honor your father and mother.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, all these I have kept since my youth.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus looked at him and loved him, and said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You lack one thing: go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But at this saying his face fell, and he went away grieving, for he had many possessions.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus looked around and said to his disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “How hard it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus said to them again,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were utterly astounded and said to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Then who can be saved?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus looked at them and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “With people it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter began to say to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, we have left everything and followed you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for my sake and for the sake of the good news

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: who will not receive a hundred times as much now in this present time (houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions) and in the age to come, eternal life.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them; they were amazed, and those who followed were afraid. Taking the twelve aside again, he began to tell them what was going to happen to him:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and they will mock him and spit on him and flog him and kill him, and after three days he will rise.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to him and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What do you want me to do for you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Grant that we may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your glory.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We can.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The cup that I drink you will drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but to sit at my right or at my left is not mine to grant; it is for those for whom it has been prepared.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the ten heard this, they began to be indignant with James and John.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus called them to him and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones wield authority over them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But it is not so among you. Rather, whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and whoever wants to be first among you will be slave of all.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came to Jericho. And as he was leaving Jericho with his disciples and a large crowd, Bartimaeus son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Many rebuked him, telling him to be silent, but he cried out all the more,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus stopped and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Call him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they called the blind man, saying to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Take courage! Get up; he is calling you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He threw off his cloak, sprang up, and came to Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What do you want me to do for you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The blind man said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Rabbouni, let me see again.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Go; your faith has saved you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And immediately he saw again, and he followed him on the road.

notes.traditional: Pharisees came up and asked him
notes.note: Many manuscripts, followed by most English versions, read 'Pharisees came up and asked him'. The SBLGNT follows witnesses that lack the phrase and leave the questioners unnamed, judging the mention of Pharisees to have been added from the parallel in Matthew 19:3. Either way the questioners are hostile, as 'testing him' shows.

In Jewish law as generally practised, only a husband could initiate a divorce; under Roman law a wife could do so as well. This half of the saying, found only in Mark, addresses that wider situation. Whether it reflects Jesus' own wording or an application for Mark's Gentile readers is debated.

The Greek can mean 'as a child receives it' or 'as one receives a child'. Most interpreters take the first; the second would link the saying with 9:37, where welcoming a child is welcoming Jesus. The rendering leaves the comparison as open as the Greek does.

The adjective is formed from the word for 'age', and in Jewish usage 'eternal life' is the life of the coming age: a matter of kind as well as length. Verse 30 makes the link audible, setting 'the age to come' beside 'eternal life'. 'Eternal' is the standard rendering and is kept here; a minority of translators render 'life of the age to come'.

This is not one of the Ten Commandments, from which the rest of the list is drawn. It may stand in for the commandment against coveting, or echo laws against withholding a worker's wages such as Deuteronomy 24:14. Why it appears here is uncertain; some suggest it is aimed at the temptations of a wealthy man.

notes.phrase: how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!
notes.traditional: how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God
notes.note: Many later manuscripts add 'for those who trust in riches', and the King James tradition follows them. The earliest witnesses lack the phrase. Most scholars think it was added to soften a saying that, in its shorter form, applies to everyone.

The Greek word meant an announcement of good news, such as a victory or a ruler's accession, and the related verb is used in the Greek Scriptures for announcing God's saving rule. 'Gospel' is the traditional rendering, but to a modern reader it suggests a book or a body of doctrine. A number of modern versions also use 'good news'.

The Greek word means 'peoples' or 'nations'; in the plural, in Jewish usage, it regularly means the non-Jewish peoples. This translation renders the one word 'Gentiles' or 'nations' according to sense. Here it refers in practice to the Roman authorities, and in verse 42 to the non-Jewish world and its rulers.

notes.phrase: be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized
notes.note: In Scripture the cup is a common image for a fate handed to someone by God, often suffering or judgment. The verb 'baptize' in ordinary Greek meant to plunge or submerge, and was used figuratively of being overwhelmed by disaster. Most interpreters take both images as pointing to Jesus' coming suffering and death, not to the rite of baptism.

The noun denotes the price paid to free a slave, a captive, or something held in pledge. The preposition translated 'for' normally means 'in place of' or 'in exchange for'. 'Many' is a Semitic way of setting the one over against the many and does not imply 'some but not all'; an echo of Isaiah 53 is widely, though not universally, recognised.

Mark leaves this Aramaic word untranslated in his Greek, and it is left so here. It is a respectful form of address meaning 'my master' or 'my teacher', a heightened form of 'Rabbi'. English versions vary between 'Rabbi', 'Master', 'Lord' and 'my teacher'.

notes.traditional: has made you well; has healed you
notes.note: The verb covers rescue from danger, healing from illness, and salvation in the fuller sense. It is the same verb as in the disciples' question in verse 26, 'Then who can be saved?' Most versions render 'made you well' or 'healed you' here, which fits the healing but hides the link. Mark may well intend both senses, since the man at once follows Jesus on the road.

candidates.reason: Occurs across the Gospels and Paul, and translators split between 'gospel' and 'good news'; readers would be misled by variation between chapters.
The same verb is used for healing, rescue and salvation, and versions vary between 'save', 'heal' and 'make well', which hides deliberate links such as 10:26 and 10:52.
Recurs throughout the New Testament with versions divided between 'slave', 'servant' and 'bondservant'; it must stay distinct from διάκονος.
Used of Judas, the priests, Pilate and God across the passion predictions and narratives, and rendered variously 'betray', 'deliver' and 'hand over', obscuring a repeated thread.
Translators alternate between 'life', 'soul' and 'self' across the New Testament, and 'soul' often imports a later body-soul dualism that needs one consistent policy.
